newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National Property plans to be NZ$100 mln company.
newsitem.headline: National Property plans to be NZ$100 mln company.

text.p: National Property Trust, which expects to list on the New Zealand Stocks Exchange on December 23, said on Tuesday it planned to become a $100 million company by gross assets in three to five years.
The company is raising $9 million via a one-for-four rights issue at 90 cents per unit and placement of four million units.
Executive chairman Paul Dallimore told reporters the company planned to grow from an asset base of $38 million following its current capital raising.

The company has agreed to buy the Hewlett Packard building in Wellington, which has a valuation of $9.8 million, and plans to buy a building of similar value next year in Auckland, Wellington or Christchurch.
Unit holders had wanted to list the trust on the NZSE to increase the liquidity of the units and to give the company greater flexibility in raising capital.
In a prospectus, NPT said it expected a net surplus after tax of $1.83 million in the year to May 1997 rising to $2.06 million in the following year.
The net surplus for the year to May 1996 was $1.02 million.
Annualised pretax returns are projected to be 10.17 cents per unit in 1997 and 10.06 cents the following year.
NPT expects indicator interest rates to fall to 8.0-8.5 percent next year but its forecasts are based on rates of 9.0 percent -- around the current average NPT is currently paying.
NPT expects to put 80 percent of its assets into commercial buildings and 20 percent into industrial. It will avoid investing in the volatile retail property market.
